body.heading: Collect fallen leaves
paragraphs: Walk with your adult and pick up leaves that have already fallen to the ground. Try to find leaves with different shapes — round ones, long ones, and ones with pointy edges.
Every kind of tree grows its own shape of leaf. The shape is like the tree's signature, written over and over again.

body.heading: Match leaf to tree
paragraphs: Stand under a tree and look up at its leaves. Do they match one of yours? Hold your leaf up and compare the shape and the edges.
Some leaves grow one by one, and some grow in groups on a single stalk. That is another clue for your matching game.

body.heading: Make a leaf line-up
paragraphs: Back home, lay your leaves in a row. Can you sort them into shape families? Draw around your favourite leaf to keep its shape forever.
Leaves that stay on the ground are not wasted. They rot down slowly and feed the soil and the tiny creatures in it.

takeaway: Each tree has its own leaf shape, so a fallen leaf can tell you which tree it came from.
safetyNotes: Only collect leaves that have already fallen. Never eat leaves or berries, and wash your hands after collecting.
screenFreeExtension: Arrange your leaves from smallest to biggest on the floor and walk along them like a leaf road.
